resolved.gap: CBSE grading - positional vs absolute (was Tier-1 blocker #2)
resolved.finding: CBSE grading is POSITIONAL for BOTH Class 10 and Class 12. Grades A-1 to D-2 each take 1/8th of the PASSED candidates in rank order; E = failed. Nine-point scale for external examination subjects; a separate FIVE-point scale (A-E) for internal assessment. Qualifying mark 33% per subject, with 33% separately in theory and practical plus 33% aggregate where practicals apply. Positional grading is used where more than 500 candidates passed the subject.
resolved.SUPERSEDES: The earlier hypothesis that Class 10 used absolute bands while Class 12 was positional. That was WRONG. Also supersedes the 'E1/E2' grade labels - CBSE has a single E.
resolved.source: CBSE 'Grading System in CBSE For 10th & 12th' and 'Scheme of Examinations and Pass Criteria' (cbse.gov.in)

resolved.gap: State board grading matrix (was Tier-1 blocker #1)
resolved.status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED - five major boards documented
resolved.finding: Pass marks range from 30% to 35% across boards (West Bengal and Karnataka 30%, CBSE and UP 33%, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu 35%). Grade MODELS differ fundamentally: positional rank (CBSE), absolute mark bands (Tamil Nadu, West Bengal), percentage plus Division (Maharashtra), inverted 1-9 (CISCE). CRITICALLY, grade labels collide: 'A1' means top-eighth-of-passers at CBSE but 91-100 marks in Tamil Nadu.
A+ 80+; A 70-79; A- 60-69; B 50-59; C 40-49; D 33-39; F below 33. Pass threshold 33% (grade D). There is NO B+ grade - seven grades total - and a full 1.00-point gap between B (3.00) and C (2.00).

resolved.formula: GPA = [ sum(grade points of compulsory subjects) + (4th-subject grade point - 2.00) ] / (number of COMPULSORY subjects)
resolved.finding: The bonus is added to the NUMERATOR while the 4th subject is EXCLUDED from the denominator, so with five compulsory subjects an A+ in the 4th subject adds +0.60 to the final GPA. The bonus applies only above 2.00. Failing the 4th subject does not affect the GPA; failing any compulsory subject drops the total to 0.00.
resolved.consequence: A GPA of 5.00 does not necessarily mean A+ in every subject, and a GPA cannot be reconstructed from subject grades without knowing the 4th-subject arrangement.

resolved.finding: Bangladesh HAS a national higher-education grading scheme: the UGC Uniform Grading Scheme, applying to all public and private universities from session 2006-2007, on a 4.00 CGPA maximum. A+ 80%+ = 4.00; A 75-<80 = 3.75; A- 70-<75 = 3.50; B+ 65-<70 = 3.25; B 60-<65 = 3.00; B- 55-<60 = 2.75; C+ 50-<55 = 2.50; C 45-<50 = 2.25; D 40-<45 = 2.00; F <40 = 0.00. Plus I (incomplete) and W (withdrawn). Regular 0.25 steps.
resolved.SUPERSEDES: The claim that Bangladeshi higher-education grading is purely institution-set with no national scheme.
resolved.caveat: A further 2022 UGC attempt at a single system 'could not be enforced due to practical and policy hurdles' - so adherence is not universal. Still read the transcript's own scale.

resolved.gap: Secondary diplomas of 9 of 13 jurisdictions (was Tier-1 blocker #6)
resolved.status: RESOLVED - all 13 jurisdictions now have a credit total
resolved.finding: Complete Canadian secondary diplomas require anywhere from 18 to 100 credits. Two useful simplifications: Yukon follows British Columbia's curriculum and graduation programme entirely, and NWT/Nunavut have historically used Alberta's course naming (though NWT is mid-transition to BC's curriculum).
resolved.key_source_discovered: CMEC publishes a per-jurisdiction Student Transfer Guide series at cmec.ca/docs/transferguide/ covering grade structures, graduation credentials, requirements, issuing authorities and grading - the single best source class for Canadian provincial detail
resolved.verification: confirmed for Ontario, BC, Quebec, New Brunswick, PEI, Newfoundland and Labrador, Manitoba; warn for the rest

resolved.gap: No pan-Canadian framework covers sub-degree qualifications
resolved.finding: Ontario operates a full 13-level Ontario Qualifications Framework (OQF) covering all non-religious postsecondary certificate, diploma and degree programs, including apprenticeship certificates. Levels: 1 Certificate I; 2 Certificate II; 3 Certificate of Apprenticeship; 4 Certificate of Qualification; 5 Certificate III (Ontario College Certificate); 6 Diploma I; 7 Diploma II (Ontario College Diploma); 8 Ontario College Advanced Diploma; 9 Post-Diploma Certificate (Ontario College Graduate Certificate); 10 Bachelor's Degree; 11 Bachelor's Degree Honours; 12 Master's Degree; 13 Doctoral Degree.
resolved.SUPERSEDES: The statement that Canada has nothing placing college diplomas relative to degrees. The correct statement is that there is no PAN-CANADIAN framework, but at least one province has one.
resolved.warning: OQF levels are Ontario's own numbering and are NOT comparable with the AQF, SCQF, RQF, BNQF, NHEQF or NCrF. An OQF level 8 Advanced Diploma is not an AQF level 8 Bachelor Honours Degree. Always name the framework alongside the level.

resolved.finding: Ontario College Certificate = two semesters (one year), OQF 5. Ontario College Diploma = at least four semesters (two years), OQF 7. Ontario College Advanced Diploma = six semesters (three years), OQF 8. Ontario College Graduate Certificate = one year or less, OQF 9 - a POST-diploma/post-degree credential ABOVE the Advanced Diploma despite the word 'certificate'.

official_volumes_of_learning.Masters Degree (Research): 1-2 years; 1.5 yr after an AQF 7 in the same discipline, 1 yr after an AQF 8, 2 yr after an AQF 7 in a different discipline

resolved.SUPERSEDES: The conflicting secondary figures for Diploma ('1.5-2 years') and Advanced Diploma ('2-3 years'). Both are REFUTED - the official figures are 1-2 and 1.5-2 respectively.

resolved.gap: The official 9-1 to A*-G GCSE comparison (was Tier-1 blocker #8)
resolved.finding: Ofqual publishes THREE anchor points, not a full mapping: the bottom of grade 7 is comparable to the bottom of the old grade A; the bottom of grade 4 to the bottom of the old grade C; the bottom of grade 1 to the bottom of the old grade G. GRADE 9 HAS NO OLD-SCALE EQUIVALENT - it was introduced to provide greater differentiation among top performers. Grades 4, 5 and 6 collectively replace the old B and C. Grade 4 is the 'standard pass', grade 5 the 'strong pass', though there is no single official pass rule for every purpose.
resolved.SUPERSEDES: The uncertain row-by-row table extracted from the UK ENIC guide, which implied 8 = A*.
resolved.ai_rule: Use the three anchors only and state explicitly that grade 9 has no old-scale equivalent. Do not construct a one-to-one mapping - Ofqual deliberately does not publish one.

resolved.gap: A level grade scale; degree classification boundaries
resolved.a_level_scale: A*, A, B, C, D, E plus U. Six passing grades plus U. A* introduced in 2010. E is the minimum pass; U means the paper did not reach E and does not count as a pass. A levels RETAINED letters while England's GCSEs moved to 9-1.

degree_classifications.caveat: Standard across most UK universities but institution-set; some institutions apply borderline or discretion rules

resolved.counselling_point: Because a UK 2:1 starts at 60%, a UK transcript showing 62% is a GOOD result - routinely misread by people from percentage systems where 60% is unremarkable.
resolved.still_open: UK master's classification conventions (Distinction / Merit / Pass) and their boundaries

resolved.status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED - and the earlier claim was too strong
resolved.finding: China's Ministry of Education announced national teaching quality standards for bachelor's degree programmes on 30 January 2018, covering 92 broad subject areas across 587 disciplines, and these DO specify credit-hours per discipline. A Chinese bachelor's typically requires 160-180 credits (MOE 2023 statistics; the standard four-year system accounts for 87.5% of national undergraduate programmes). The hours-per-credit conversion is institution-set - one reported convention is one 45-minute class hour per week over an ~18-week semester.
resolved.SUPERSEDES: The claim that no national Chinese credit specification exists. The correct statement is that there is no single national credit-to-notional-hours FORMULA comparable to India's 30 hours or Bangladesh's 40.
resolved.consequence: This makes the cross-country credit warning sharper: a Chinese 160-180 credit bachelor's, a US 120-credit bachelor's, a UK 360-credit bachelor's and an Indian 120-credit bachelor's are all first degrees whose credit numbers differ by up to a factor of three because the units are entirely different.

resolved.finding: China issues THREE categories of Higher Education Qualification Certificate: regular higher education, adult higher education, and self-taught examination. Crucially, the different study modes are INDICATED ON THE CERTIFICATES THEMSELVES, so the AI does not have to infer the route. Four forms of adult continuing education exist: the adult university entrance exam, self-taught higher education examinations, TV university modern open distance education, and online education. The self-taught route (zikao) has an entirely open enrolment policy accepting applicants from all backgrounds and academic levels, with candidates registering with a provincial Self-taught Higher Education Examinations Committee and completing at their own pace.
resolved.ai_rule: Ask the student to read the certificate's own wording. All three categories are CHSI-verifiable and nationally recognised; describe the route neutrally and accurately, and do not rank it.

resolved.gap: Community college to university transfer and articulation (was Tier-2 #11, the largest US gap)
resolved.finding: At least 31 states have policies requiring a transferable core of lower-division courses AND statewide guaranteed transfer of an associate degree. States are increasingly setting statewide credit transfer requirements rather than relying on institution-level agreements. Documented examples: North Carolina's Comprehensive Articulation Agreement between the NC Community College System and the UNC System; Florida, where completing an Associate in Arts at any Florida state college guarantees admission to one of Florida's 12 public universities; Colorado's GT Pathways and 'Degrees with Designation'; Hawaii's Automatic Admission program for the seven UH community colleges.
caveats: It usually attaches to a particular degree type - typically the Associate in Arts (AA), not the applied AAS
19 or more states have no such statewide policy, so transfer there is institution-by-institution
resolved.authoritative_source: Education Commission of the States, '50-State Comparison: Transfer and Articulation Policies' (ecs.org/50-state-comparison-transfer-and-articulation/) - a single source covering all 50 states

resolved.gap: NEB grade boundaries and pass criteria (Tier-1 blocker #3)
resolved.status: NOT RESOLVED - and the conflict WIDENED
resolved.finding: A fourth variant of the pass criteria emerged and directly contradicts the first: it states a per-subject minimum of grade D (35%, GPA 1.6) AND an overall GPA of 2.0 (50%) to pass. The earlier Claim A stated there is NO aggregate minimum. Both come from Nepali education sources. The AI must NOT state an aggregate requirement.
resolved.what_was_established: The Letter Grading Directive 2078's contents are now documented: issued by MoEST for Classes 1-12, developed in line with the National Curriculum Framework 2076, and it defines credit hour, letter grading and grade point, specifies how internal, practical and theoretical assessment marks convert to letter grades, and covers grade categories, achievement levels, grade improvement examinations, certification requirements and the roles of the Ministry, CDC, NEB, Education Development and Coordination Units and schools. This confirms the directive is the correct authority for everything currently marked warn.
resolved.new_finding_requiring_verification: A source states that NEB results show ONLY letter grades and that numerical marks are not included in official results. If correct this is operationally important - a Nepali student may have no percentage to report - but it conflicts with the 75-theory/25-internal marks structure documented elsewhere. Confirm at NEB what an official Grade 12 grade sheet displays.

anti_fabrication.rule: Never compare raw credit counts across countries.
anti_fabrication.why: A credit is 10 notional hours in the UK (CATS/SCQF), 25-30 in ECTS, 30 in India (NCrF), 40 in Bangladesh (BNQF, lecture-based), and approximately 45 in the US (34 CFR 600.2). Canada's CDQF and China define no notional-hour value at all.
anti_fabrication.instead: Reason in years of full-time study or notional hours, state the assumption, and defer the formal judgement to the destination institution or a recognised evaluator.

anti_fabrication.rule: Never convert a GPA between scales, or into a foreign scale.
anti_fabrication.why: Scales in play across these eight countries include 4.0 (two structurally different variants in Nepal alone), 5.00 (Bangladesh school), 10-point (India higher education), 7-point (Australia), 4.0/4.3/4.33/9-point/12-point (Canada), and weighted GPAs above 4.0 (US high school).
anti_fabrication.instead: Report each figure with its scale, maximum, document and institution. Where a conversion is needed, use the issuing institution's own conversion certificate (common in India) or the destination's published method.

anti_fabrication.rule: Never convert a rank or an examination score into a grade or percentage.
Only one officially published grade conversion was found in this entire research project.
anti_fabrication.detail: CBSE's x 9.5 conversion from the Class 10 CGPA (approximately 2011-2017 era) to a percentage. Every other conversion the AI might be tempted to apply is unofficial.

anti_fabrication.rule: Do not assert a qualification framework level for a country that has none.
anti_fabrication.note: The absence was not positively confirmed from an official source for the US or China. Priority gap.

first_questions_by_country.Nepal: Which year did you study (pre- or post-2016)? Which board issued the Grade 12 award - NEB, or Cambridge/IB? Which university awarded your degree, and was it 3 or 4 years?
first_questions_by_country.India: WHICH BOARD? Which year? Was your bachelor's degree 3 or 4 years, and how many credits?
first_questions_by_country.Bangladesh: Which board (general regional / BMEB madrasah / BTEB technical)? Is the GPA on the 5.00 school scale or a 4.00 university scale? Was your bachelor's 3, 4 or 5 years?
first_questions_by_country.China (mainland): How many years was the programme (2-3 = zhuanke, 4-5 = benke)? Do you have BOTH a graduation certificate and a degree certificate? Which province and year for the gaokao?
first_questions_by_country.Australia: Which state or territory (which Year 12 certificate)? Is the figure an ATAR (a rank), a GPA (out of 7) or a WAM (a percentage)? Was 'Honours' integrated or a standalone year?
first_questions_by_country.Canada: WHICH PROVINCE OR TERRITORY? Was it Quebec (DES + CEGEP + 3-year degree)? What is the GPA scale maximum?
first_questions_by_country.United Kingdom: WHICH UK NATION? (GCSE grading, year numbering and degree length all differ.) Honours or Ordinary, and what classification? Which university (for a Scottish 'MA')?
first_questions_by_country.United States: Which state? Is the GPA weighted or unweighted, high school or college? Is the institution accredited by a USDE/CHEA-recognised accreditor?

highest_risk_facts.fact: An 'MA (Hons)' from Aberdeen, Edinburgh, Glasgow or St Andrews is an UNDERGRADUATE degree (SCQF 10 / FHEQ 6).
China issues TWO separate documents for higher education - a graduation certificate and a degree certificate - and either can be missing.
School GPA is on a 5.00 scale while university CGPA is typically 4.00. A student legitimately holds both.
Quebec secondary education ends at Secondary V, which 'corresponds to grade 11 in other jurisdictions'; CEGEP follows; a Quebec bachelor's degree is typically 3 years and is complete.
The ATAR is a rank (0.00-99.95), not a mark. An ATAR of 70 means the top 30% of the cohort.

Both 3-year (120-credit, NHEQF 5.5) and 4-year Honours (160-credit, NHEQF 6) bachelor's degrees are currently awarded, and '(Hons)' is ambiguous between the pre-NEP 3-year specialised degree and the NEP 4-year degree.
Northern Ireland's school year numbering is offset by one from England's - NI Year 12 is the GCSE year.
A high school GPA above 4.0 is a weighted GPA; college transcripts report the unweighted figure.
'SLC' means the Grade 10 exam pre-2016 and the Grade 12 exam in NQF policy language.

Professional medical/law qualifications are placed at OPPOSITE framework levels: Canada's CDQF calls MD/DDS/JD 'bachelor's programs in academic standing'; the UK places MB BS/BDS at FHEQ 7 (master's level); Australia reportedly classifies JD/MD as AQF 9 Masters (Extended); the US has no framework level to state.

school_boards.detail: NEB is the only general-education school board. Plus CTEVT (vocational) as a parallel stream. NO provincial school boards.

qualification_framework.descriptor_basis: Learning outcomes; cites SAQA (South Africa) 2013 and ILO
qualification_framework.isced_note: ISCED levels 4 and 5 are NOT used in the framework's mapping.

qualification_framework.implementation: Partial; NVQF reported as implemented up to NVQ Level 5

'(Hons)' is ambiguous - pre-NEP 3-year specialised honours vs NEP 4-year Honours (160 credits). Ask the duration.

countries.recognition_test: For school qualifications: was it issued by one of the 11 boards? For higher education: is the awarding university UGC-approved? For technical awards: is the institution BTEB-affiliated?
distinctive_features: The 4th-subject GPA rule: an optional fourth subject contributes (its grade point - 2.0), never below zero. A reported GPA cannot be reverse-engineered from subject grades.
Dual certification: SSC (Voc) confers both an SSC and an NSC 3; HSC (Voc)/(BMT) confers both an HSC and an NSC 5.
The BTEB Diploma is 4 years at BNQF Level 6 - a level ABOVE the HSC - and explicitly 'interfaces with the HE qualifications'.
A 1-year master's is normal (BNQF Level 9 permits 1-2 years; a coursework master's requires only 40 credits).
Notional hours per credit differ by activity type (40/60/80), so a 4-credit subject can represent 160-320 notional hours.

atar.nature: A RANK, not a mark or score
atar.meaning: the holder's percentile position out of all students completing the certificate in that year, within their age group
atar.worked_example: An ATAR of 75.00 means results higher than, or as well as, 75 per cent of all students in that year. An ATAR of 70 means the top 30 per cent.
atar.scaling: Subject marks are SCALED before aggregation, 'which allows a fair comparison of students who have studied different combinations of courses'
atar.admission_figure: Admission to most tertiary courses uses the SELECTION RANK = ATAR + any applicable adjustments
atar.must_not: Never convert an ATAR into a percentage or a GPA

ai_rules: The ATAR is a rank, not a mark - never convert it.
A Bachelor Honours Degree is AQF Level 8, a level ABOVE Bachelor Degree (AQF 7), at the same level as a Graduate Certificate/Diploma.
Eight different Year 12 certificates, one AQF position - record which, treat as the same level.
The 7-point GPA and the WAM are two different measures, and neither is a 4.0 GPA.
HD/D/C/P boundaries are institution-set - an HD may start at 80% or 85%.
'Kindergarten' means the first year of school in NSW/ACT but pre-school elsewhere.
Australian VET is competency-based, not graded.
A Statement of Attainment is NOT a qualification - it certifies some units only.
Non-ATAR entry (VET, portfolio, mature-age, bridging, Diploma pathways) is institutionalised, not exceptional.

countries.governance_note: Under the 10th Amendment, and because the Constitution never mentions education, states hold primary legal authority. Federal statutes prohibit the federal government from 'mandating, directing, or controlling' instructional content or curriculum. 50 states + DC + territories, with further district-level variation. Colorado, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania allow local districts to determine most or all graduation requirements.

qualification_framework.name: NONE
qualification_framework.detail: The US has no numbered national level framework, no national level descriptors, no national qualification-type register, and no national body that places a qualification on a level.
qualification_framework.note: The absence was NOT positively confirmed from an official source - priority gap. A voluntary non-governmental instrument (the Degree Qualifications Profile) has been promoted, and some states have their own frameworks.
what_exists_instead: the federally defined credit hour (34 CFR 600.2)
de facto degree conventions (60-credit associate, 120-credit bachelor's, 4.0 GPA, A-F grades)

credit_hour.definition_verbatim: a credit hour is an amount of student work defined by an institution, as approved by the institution's accrediting agency or State approval agency, that is consistent with commonly accepted practice in postsecondary education and that (1) Reasonably approximates not less than (i) One hour of classroom or direct faculty instruction and a minimum of two hours of out-of-class student work each week for approximately fifteen weeks for one semester or trimester hour of credit, or ten to twelve weeks for one quarter hour of credit, or the equivalent amount of work over a different period of time; or (ii) At least an equivalent amount of work as required in paragraph (1)(i) of this definition for other academic activities as established by the institution, including laboratory work, internships, practica, studio work, and other academic work leading to the award of credit hours; and (2) Permits an institution, in determining the amount of work associated with a credit hour, to take into account a variety of delivery methods, measurements of student work, academic calendars, disciplines, and degree levels.
credit_hour.carnegie_unit: The definition 'approximates the original time-based Carnegie unit' but requires evaluation against 'intended learning outcomes' and 'evidence of student achievement'. High school 'credits' are Carnegie-unit based and are a DIFFERENT unit from college credit hours.

high_school_diploma.warning: A US high school credit count is uninterpretable without the state. A diploma earned with 13 credits and one earned with 40 credits are BOTH complete diplomas.
high_school_diploma.diploma_types: Many states issue more than one diploma type (standard / advanced / alternative) - NOT researched

admission.tests: SAT or ACT - privately administered ADMISSION TESTS, not qualifications; many institutions now test-optional
admission.international: institution-specific; often a NACES-member evaluation of foreign credentials
admission.existing_globaly_kb_quote: 'recognition is decentralized. Universities evaluate credentials in-house or require a NACES-member evaluation (WES, ECE, etc.). Requirements are institution-specific.'

ai_rules: There is no US qualifications framework - describe by type, credits, duration, entry requirement and accreditation, and never assert a level.
A high school GPA above 4.0 is weighted; a college GPA on a transcript is unweighted.
High school credit requirements range from 13 to 40 across states - a raw count says nothing without the state.
'Diploma' in US usage means the certificate document, not a sub-degree qualification.
'College' means higher education in the US - the opposite of the Nepal/Bangladesh/UK/Canada senses.
'Accredited' means accredited by a USDE/CHEA-recognised accreditor - a real and occasionally failed test.
The federally defined credit hour (~45 notional hours per semester credit) must not be equated with UK, ECTS, Indian or Bangladeshi credits.
'Freshman/sophomore/junior/senior' are ambiguous between high school and college.
